issues: The predicate adds an unsupported exclusion requiring is_party=false. The quoted definition does not exclude the referenced party from Affiliate status; it covers any individual or entity having a specified Control relationship with that party.

Case out_party_itself expressly states that the party Controls itself, which satisfies the proposed controls_party fact and the quoted Control-relationship limb, but the predicate rejects it solely because is_party=true.

Case out_party_controlled does not state that the candidate is Controlled by the referenced party. It instead states that the party is Controlled by another entity. Therefore its controlled_by_party=true coding is unsupported by its fact text.

The quoted definition incorporates the capitalized term Control, but the required Section 1.3 definition is not supplied. The listed ownership and policy-control concepts are not present in the quote and cannot substitute for the missing attachment.
The predicate and its stated biconditional faithfully reproduce the quoted definition at the rule level.

The positive case texts state advertised start, viewing, or screening times for feature films, but do not explicitly state that the relevant time is an advertised 'showtime.' Treating every such time as a showtime requires an unstated ordinary-meaning gloss.

The non-feature-film cases identify a short documentary, news program, live concert, or guided tour, but do not expressly state that the item is not a feature film. Their false coding therefore depends on an unsupplied definition or classification of 'feature film.'

The program expressly identifies ordinary meanings of 'feature film' and 'advertised' as dependencies, but supplies neither definitions nor authoritative attachments resolving them. The source quote alone does not establish all classifications used by the cases.
No exception or additional condition appears in the quoted definition, but the case vectors must be rewritten to state the coded conjunction or its negation explicitly.

The quoted definition relies on the capitalized term "Laws," but its definition or governing attachment is not provided. This prevents verification of the scope of "Laws" and potentially of "governmental authority having jurisdiction."
No case covers the listed asset type "trade_name," although this is a test-coverage gap rather than a mismatch between the supplied case text and coded facts.

The predicate incorrectly requires the candidate Person to also be the Party. The definition instead covers any Person that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with the specified Party.

The source requires a control relationship to the specified Party: controls the Party, is controlled by the Party, or is under common control with the Party. The fields and predicate capture only a person's possession of control power or ownership, without identifying the direction of control, the controlled Person, or a common controlling Person.

The predicate makes 'through one or more intermediaries' mandatory for every alternative. The source permits control directly or indirectly; intermediaries are a possible means of indirect control, not a separately mandatory condition.

The foreign-law proviso is misimplemented. It substitutes the legally permitted lower ownership percentage for the more-than-50-percent ownership threshold, provided the foreign investor has management/policy power. The predicate tests only that the legal maximum is below 50% and that power exists; it does not test ownership of the applicable lower percentage.

The foreign-law field is not sufficient to establish the required ownership threshold. Although some fact texts state 40% ownership and a 40% legal maximum, the structured facts have no scoped field establishing that ownership equals or satisfies the applicable substituted threshold.

Ownership, control power, foreign-entity status, and the relevant Party/entity are not target-scoped. In particular, c11's 60% ownership of 'another entity' sets the general ownership field true even though it is not stated to concern the foreign entity or the relevant Party.

The cases do not establish that Party B, the foreign entity, or another referenced entity is a Person, nor do they identify which entity is the specified Party and which is the candidate Affiliate. These are material facts under the definition.
c12 and c13 contain internally inconsistent assertions ('is a Party' / 'is a Person' followed by the corresponding negation), so their Boolean vectors cannot unambiguously represent the stated facts.

c14 both states that Party A acts directly through an intermediary and states that Party A does not act directly or indirectly; its direct_or_indirect=false vector conflicts with the earlier affirmative statement.

c15 both states action through one intermediary and states that Party A does not act through any intermediaries; its through_intermediaries=false vector conflicts with the earlier affirmative statement.

Definitions of 'Party' and 'Person' are identified as dependencies but are not supplied. More importantly, the source and cases lack the external/entity-specific facts needed to determine the required control relationship.
The predicate omits the express threshold that the Customer must be a person or business entity; it would classify any otherwise qualifying non-person/non-business candidate as a Customer.

The source's final qualifier, "pursuant to this Agreement," is not syntactically assigned expressly to the agreement rather than the purchase/transaction. The program makes it an agreement-specific fact without support resolving that scope.
The governing "this Agreement" is not provided. Its operative terms, applicability, and any qualifications affecting what can be pursuant to it cannot be audited.

The incorporated definitions are referenced by section number but are not supplied as complete contract text. The abbreviated dependency descriptions cannot establish that no further limitations or exceptions apply.
In out_no_agreement, the text says Epsilon received Products, not that an agreement for Products or Services existed; nevertheless agreement_subject_products_or_services is coded true.

In out_no_agreement_no_purchase and out_no_agreement_not_pursuant, the text expressly denies that Distributor entered an agreement for Products/Services, while agreement_subject_products_or_services is coded true.
Several no-agreement cases use "matter" or a purchase as the thing that is or is not pursuant to the Agreement, rather than explicitly stating the coded agreement-specific pursuant fact.

Case in_kfda_agency states a disjunctive fact (the entity is the Korean Food and Drug Administration or a successor agency thereto) but codes the specific entity_type value Korean Food and Drug Administration. The text does not explicitly establish that selected value rather than the successor-agency alternative.
The definition itself is sufficient and the predicate correctly includes both expressly defined alternatives: the Korean Food and Drug Administration and any successor agency thereto.

The source definition requires that the relevant party be 'a reseller.' The predicate has no reseller-status element, and no case text explicitly states that the named entity is a reseller. Authorization, agreement party status, and permission to purchase and resell do not exactly establish that separate definitional condition.

The listed dependency on the ordinary meaning of 'reseller' confirms that reseller status is an external or unprovided factual/legal determination. No attachment, definition, or case fact supplies it, so the source and case materials are insufficient for a complete application of the proposed rule.

In c08, the text says Theta is authorized to purchase and resell but expressly says Cisco did not enter an authorization agreement with Theta. It does not state that an agreement authorizes those acts, yet both agreement-authorization fields are coded true. Those coded facts therefore do not match the text.
The remaining agreement-related fields generally track the stated authorization-agreement conditions, but they cannot cure the omitted reseller-status requirement.
The predicate faithfully reflects the two enumerated disjuncts in the quoted definition: the seven listed roles of Vendor, or the five listed roles of a Vendor contractor or Subcontractor.

The fatal exclusion-case vectors code role_with_vendor_contractor_or_subcontractor as "none," but their texts do not explicitly state that the individual has none of the five enumerated roles with a Vendor contractor or Subcontractor. Being a contractor of a Vendor contractor/Subcontractor, a customer of Vendor, or a shareholder of Vendor does not itself exclude also being an officer, director, employee, representative, or agent of a Vendor contractor or Subcontractor.

The quoted source relies on absent definitions or contextual determinations for "Vendor," capitalized "Subcontractor," and potentially "contractor." Those dependencies prevent complete application of the rule to real facts without the referenced agreement material.
The quoted definition makes Board mean the board of directors of the Company, and the conjunction of being a board of directors and being of the Company faithfully reflects that definition.

The source window does not include the definition or identity of "Company." This is an external dependency needed to apply the term outside the stipulated case facts, although the cases expressly state the relevant Company relationship.
All case fact vectors are explicitly supported by their accompanying fact text for the two coded fields.

Cases c11 and c12 are internally contradictory: each states that services are provided to an entity in the United Arab Emirates, then states that the entity is not in the United Arab Emirates. The coded UAE-recipient value cannot be conclusively set to false from contradictory text.

Cases c13 and c14 are internally contradictory: each states that services are provided to an entity in the United Arab Emirates, then states that the services are not provided to any entity. The coded UAE-recipient value cannot be conclusively set to false from contradictory text.

The predicate faithfully reflects the quoted definition: qualifying services must be nuclear consulting or strategic advisory services, and those services must be provided to an entity in the United Arab Emirates.

The source separately includes a company 'owned ... by' CERES, but defines only 'control' as more-than-50% voting ownership or director-nomination power. The predicate treats ownership as qualifying only when it exceeds 50%, without establishing that all lesser ownership interests are excluded from 'owned by.'

Accordingly, cases stating that CERES owns 10% or 40% of the entity cannot be conclusively excluded under the supplied source text. The source does not define the ownership threshold or scope for the independent 'owned by' limb.
The supplied quote is insufficient to derive an exact Boolean predicate that excludes partial ownership absent control; an unprovided definition of 'owned' or contractual context would be required.

The source requires a contract 'pursuant to which' the specified benefits are provided or received. The predicate only requires that a contract exists and that the benefit relationships exist; it does not require that those relationships arise pursuant to the contract.

The four purported in-scope case texts state a contract and separately state benefit relationships, but do not explicitly state that the benefits are provided or received pursuant to that contract. Their inclusion cannot be established from the stated facts.

The separate third_party_involved condition is redundant if the coded benefit-relation field is true, because that field itself requires a benefit to or from a third party. This is not the principal defect, but it introduces an unnecessary independent condition not separately expressed by the definition.

Case out_former_customer states that Nu is a former Allscripts customer, but codes is_customer as true. Former-customer status does not explicitly establish current customer status and ordinarily contradicts it.

The same case distinguishes no current contract from the program's unqualified has_contracted_for_allscripts_products_or_services field. The source definition does not limit contracting to current contracts, so this temporal recoding is unsupported.

The predicate's second branch treats any instrument marked is_supplement_or_reissue=true as a Tariff, without requiring that it be a supplement to or reissue of a qualifying intrastate or interstate tariff. The source includes only supplements and reissues 'thereto'—i.e., of the described tariffs—not supplements or reissues of arbitrary instruments.

Consequently, the predicate would classify a supplement or reissue of a contract, policy manual, or other non-tariff instrument as a Tariff if the remaining conditions are met. This is broader than the source definition.

The field is_supplement_or_reissue does not encode the required relationship to an intrastate/interstate tariff. It must instead establish that the instrument is a supplement to or reissue of a qualifying tariff, or instrument_type must retain the underlying tariff classification for supplements/reissues.

c03, c11, and c13 state that the instrument is a supplement to an intrastate tariff but code instrument_type as contract. This contradicts the stated tariff relationship and permits the flawed second predicate branch to supply eligibility independently of the underlying tariff.

c04 and c12 state that the instrument is a reissue of an interstate tariff but code instrument_type as policy_manual. This contradicts the stated tariff relationship and likewise masks the required relationship to an interstate tariff.

The update branch is overbroad. The source covers only modifications or updates 'to it,' i.e., to the specified qualifying Google Toolbar binary code; the predicate requires only that something be a modification or update provided by Google to Distributor, without representing or testing that required relationship.

The fact schema has no field establishing that a modification or update is to the specified Google Toolbar binary code version. Consequently, the omitted source limitation cannot be evaluated, and updates to another product can satisfy the predicate.

Several vectors contradict their text. For example, base_binary_provided, base_binary_not_provided, base_binary_wrong_browser, and base_binary_not_machine_readable state that Google provided the item to Distributor but code was_provided_by_google_to_distributor as false.

Several update cases describe an update to the Google toolbar for Internet Explorer while coding is_google_toolbar_for_internet_explorer as false, including update_provided_by_google and update_provided_by_google_to_distributor. If the field is intended to apply only to the original binary code rather than the update target, its label and source basis do not state that distinction.

Many false-valued facts are not explicitly stated in their case text, particularly whether the item is or is not a modification/update, whether it is machine-readable binary code, and whether provision occurred in connection with the Agreement. Absence of a statement is not an explicit false fact.

The vectors conflate facts about separate objects or events. In binary_and_update_both_provided, the base binary and an update are distinct items, but the flat fields simultaneously describe one apparent item as both the binary code version and a modification/update. The required 'update to it' linkage is not encoded.

Cases involving other products demonstrate the rule defect: an update to a different Google product is coded as a Google-provided update and would satisfy the update predicate despite being excluded by 'to it.'

The predicate does not separately model the final inclusion clause, "including, without limitation, any Combination Product." Conservatively, that clause may expand Product beyond pharmaceutical products satisfying the stated active-ingredient condition; the supplied Combination Product definition is absent, so its exact effect and scope cannot be confirmed.

The cited external dependencies are not supplied: definitions of pharmaceutical product, active ingredient, and Combination Product, plus the referenced identities/naming of Binimetinib and Encorafenib. These may control boundary cases and whether a product qualifies.

Case c04 states that the item is a Combination Product, but there is no corresponding coded field. This does not alter its proposed outcome because its other explicitly coded facts satisfy the predicate, but it prevents testing the purported Combination Product inclusion independently.
The quoted definition depends on absent definitions or factual determinations for “Marketing Approvals,” “Regulatory Authorities,” “pharmaceutical product,” and the relevant regulatory jurisdiction.

The predicate treats “of all applicable Regulatory Authorities” as issuance by one applicable Regulatory Authority. The source language may instead require approvals from every authority applicable to the product/activity; the supplied text does not resolve this.

The single boolean necessary_for_listed_activity does not capture the source’s precise necessity relationship to the enumerated activities, product, and jurisdiction. In particular, the text does not expressly establish whether necessity for one activity suffices or whether a broader set of necessary approvals is required.
The program’s broad rule summary (“a listed commercialization activity”) is a plausible interpretation but is not an exact conclusion supported by the quoted definition alone.

The predicate improperly makes legal_basis_is_covered a required conjunct. In the source, 'whether based on contract, tort, statute or other legal or equitable theory' is a broad, non-exclusive characterization of controversies or claims, not an express condition excluding a stated controversy merely because it is described as non-legal.

The source's operative scope is any controversy or claim arising out of or related to the Agreement (including amendments or extensions), or concerning its breach or termination. Thus the listed cases that expressly state a controversy or claim and the required Agreement connection or breach/termination are within the definition even when legal_basis_is_covered is false.
All case texts expressly provide the coded Boolean facts, and no external attachment or redacted source fact is needed to evaluate the rule.

The source says Products that require "special testing, packaging or otherwise to be modified"; it does not expressly say "special packaging." The proposed field, predicate, summary, and case language add the qualifier "special" to packaging, which is a plausible ellipsis but not an exact textual rule.

The clause's compressed grammar should be preserved or expressly resolved: the program treats JRVS written approval as required only for Distributor-requested modifications. That is likely the intended reading, but the source should be operationalized with the source's exact phrasing or supported by drafting context if exactness is required.

The predicate makes delivery by Operator to Owner a universal requirement. The source places that delivery language within the clause concerning corrections, improvements, and enhancements to the Bloom Systems; it does not unambiguously impose delivery on every listed material, document, notebook, form, diagram, manual, written material, or tangible object. A universal-delivery gloss is therefore not an exact rule.

The coded correction/improvement/enhancement field is unused by the predicate, despite the source expressly including those items. The program does not model the potentially distinct inclusion-and-delivery condition for those items.
c09 and c12 are rejected solely because delivery by Operator to Owner is false, although the source text does not clearly require such delivery for ordinary Training Materials.

Several case vectors code `is_correction_improvement_or_enhancement_to_bloom_systems:false` without the case text expressly stating that negative fact, including c01-c04 and c08-c12. Absence of a statement that an item is a correction, improvement, or enhancement is not an explicit negative fact.

Some `is_written_material_or_tangible_object:true` or false codings rely on characterization or inference from labels such as 'manual,' 'notebook,' 'diagram,' or 'intangible service,' rather than each case expressly stating the full coded disjunctive fact.

The predicate incorrectly makes lack of authorization to resell a definitional element of "Business Entity." The source defines a Business Entity by entity type, acquisition from a Channel Partner, and use by employees and contractors; the separate sentence states a consequence or restriction applicable to a Business Entity, not an additional condition for qualifying as one.
The rule summary's "if and only if" formulation likewise incorrectly incorporates the resale prohibition into the definition.

Cases out_no_acquire and out_corp_no_acquire_authorized state only that the entity does not acquire Services from Channel Partner for use by employees and contractors. They do not explicitly establish the separately coded fact services_for_use_by_employees_and_contractors=true; without an acquisition, that independent use-purpose fact is not stated.

The source expressly relies on undefined external terms, "Services" and "Channel Partner," but their definitions are not provided. Those missing attachments may affect the scope of acquisition and therefore prevent a fully self-contained exact implementation.
The predicate faithfully mirrors the stated conjunctive definition; no exceptions or additional conditions appear in the supplied source quote.

c03 states only that the material was published by a third party rather than Licensor. It does not explicitly state that Licensor did not make the material available, so the coded false value for the combined published_or_made_available_by_licensor field is not established.

c04 states publication by Licensor occurred before the term, but does not explicitly exclude Licensor making the material available during the term. Therefore its coded during_term=false treatment of the source's publication-or-availability-during-term condition is not fully supported.

c07 states third-party availability outside the term, but does not expressly exclude separate Licensor publication or availability, including during the term. Its false values for the Licensor and term conditions are consequently underdetermined.

The Customer definition, Licensed Product definition, Exhibit A, Licensor identity, and Agreement term are identified as dependencies but are not supplied. In particular, Exhibit A is an absent required attachment for determining the scope of Licensed Products.
The quoted definition itself supports the four conjunctive predicate elements and contains no additional stated exception or alternative path.

The referenced definitions of "Party," "Agreement," and "Service" are not supplied. Those attachments are necessary to determine who contractually qualifies as a Party and any scope limitations, although the supplied case narratives expressly stipulate Party status.

The predicate incorrectly requires `is_related_to_platform` for both alternatives. The source limits the 'related to the platform' qualifier to normative documents noticed to Party B by Party A by E-mail or other means; the separate alternative covers various normative documents published on the platform without expressly requiring that they be related to the platform.

The referenced Definition of Platform (1.1) and the identities/defined roles of Party A and Party B are not supplied. These omissions prevent verification of the incorporated terms, although the quoted sentence is sufficient to identify the predicate's structural error.

Case 09's text says Party A noticed the document to Party B 'but not by E-mail or other means.' While the coded booleans are expressly stated, this is linguistically anomalous because 'other means' ordinarily encompasses any non-email notice method.

The source defines Users as subscribers to "Licensee's services," but the predicate substitutes the narrower and unprovided criterion that the relevant service is "owned by Licensee." Ownership is not stated in the source and is not necessarily equivalent to being Licensee's services.

The required definitions or scope materials for "Licensee," "Licensee's services," and "subscribers" are identified as dependencies but are not supplied. Those materials may define inclusions, exclusions, affiliates, trials, corporate accounts, resellers, campus programs, or other exceptions.
The case fact vectors are consistent with their individual fact text, but their use of service ownership cannot be validated against the quoted definition alone.

The predicate adds an unsupported requirement that the Rule 424(b) or (c) prospectus be filed after the Registration Statement initially became effective. The source compares the prospectus with the prospectus on file at initial effectiveness, but does not impose a post-effectiveness filing condition.

The source makes the defined-term substitution effective 'from and after the time said prospectus is filed with the Commission.' This is an operative timing rule for when the replacement prospectus is referred to as 'Prospectus,' not a requirement that its filing occur after initial effectiveness.

Accordingly, out_before_effective states all source conditions for the exception (Company filer, Rule 424(b), differing prospectus, and Commission filing) and should not be excluded merely because its filing was before initial effectiveness.

The source defines Confidential Information to include proprietary information as well as trade secrets and confidential information. The program has no field or predicate branch expressly covering proprietary information that is neither a trade secret nor confidential information; treating it as a plausible subset of the named field is not an exact implementation.

Section 7 is incorporated by reference to determine when the Agreement-existence item is excepted, but Section 7 is not supplied. Therefore the source is insufficient to determine or validate the permitted_by_section_7 condition, including the two existence-of-agreement cases.
The fact vectors otherwise match their case texts: every coded Boolean is expressly stated or directly entailed by the stated facts.

The predicate omits the source's threshold requirement that the receiving party 'can demonstrate with competent written proof' before any of the five exclusions applies. Instead, it treats each exclusion fact as dispositive even where competent_written_proof is false.

The required-disclosure provision is inverted. Under the source, required disclosure is an exclusion only when competent written proof exists and prompt written notice is given and scope is limited to the extent possible. The proposed predicate instead creates affirmative inclusion branches for required disclosures with notice and limited scope, while excluding required disclosures lacking those conditions.

The third-party branch is not an exact rendering of 'any information described in this Section which either party obtains from a third party under an obligation of confidentiality.' It discards the preceding described-information qualifications (including disclosure during the term, oral/written form, and confidentiality/proprietary identification) without textual support. At minimum, the source wording is not sufficient to support this broader independent branch as an exact rule.

Every case codes competent_written_proof as false, but no case text explicitly states that the receiving party lacks competent written proof. This is material because proof is required for each exclusion.

Several cases additionally code facts false without expressly stating them. For example, the third-party scenarios do not expressly establish that the information was not disclosed during the term, was not in oral or written form, or was not marked/reasonably identified; a fact not being mentioned is not an express negation.

Cases c04, c05, and c14 encode legally required disclosures as predicate-qualifying inclusion situations, contrary to the source's conditional exclusion structure. Cases c06-c10 and c13 also cannot be evaluated as exclusions as coded because the necessary competent-written-proof condition is expressly coded false but not textually stated.

The definition of "Event" is limited to "the FLOODfest Event at the Virgin Hotel Chicago." The separate following sentence states that the Event is scheduled on specified dates; it does not expressly make those dates conjunctive conditions of the defined term. The proposed predicate improperly treats start_date and end_date as necessary elements of the definition.
The rule summary likewise converts a stated scheduling attribute into an exclusive definitional requirement.

The source defines Indication as "treatment" but does not expressly limit treatment to therapeutic intervention or expressly exclude prophylaxis. The predicate's therapeutic-only requirement is therefore not an exact textual rule without the identified external semantic dependency.
The program itself identifies unresolved dependencies concerning the meaning of treatment; no source material resolving those dependencies is supplied.
Case c10 states that the subject is "A human" but codes subject_species as "unknown" and simultaneously says the species is not stated. This directly contradicts the case text.

The agent_context value no_product is used both where no intervention/product is present and where a product exists but is unnamed; although agent context is not predicate-relevant, this is not a consistently explicit fact encoding.

The predicate faithfully implements the stated disjunction: an enumerated entity type is an Affiliate when it controls the Party, is controlled by the Party, or is under common control, with control defined by at least 50% direct or indirect beneficial voting ownership or effective management appointment/dismissal power.

Several ownership facts use 'owns' rather than the source's required 'beneficial ownership.' Direct ownership is not an exact explicit statement of beneficial ownership under a conservative audit: in_party_voting_50 and in_entity_voting_60 therefore do not expressly support their true voting-control codes.

The 49% and 49.9% negative ownership cases do not expressly negate all possible direct and indirect beneficial ownership at or above 50%. Stating one direct or indirect holding below 50% does not exclude additional holdings or another ownership route: out_party_owns_49, out_entity_owns_49, and out_boundary_49_9.
out_common_control_third_party denies only direct voting and management control between Party A and Entity L. The source includes indirect control, which is not expressly negated.

out_management_control_different_entity expressly denies Party A's management power over Entity M and Entity M's ownership/control of Party A, but does not deny Party A's direct or indirect beneficial voting ownership of Entity M. Its false party_voting_control code is unsupported.
No external attachment, incorporated definition, score, or redacted fact is necessary to interpret the quoted Affiliate definition.

The operative predicate and all coded case distinctions faithfully reflect the quoted Seizure definition, including the exclusion of prevention of release of an intermediate product containing the Product.

The quoted definition relies on the externally defined terms “Applicable Regulatory Authority” and “Product.” Those definitions are identified as dependencies but are not supplied, so the source is insufficient to verify the full contractual scope of those terms.

The delivered-content branch incorrectly requires is_sponsor_advertising_content=true. The source says delivered proprietary content 'including, Sponsor Advertising Content'; 'including' is non-exclusive and does not restrict Content to Sponsor Advertising Content.

Consequently, non-Sponsor proprietary content delivered by a party to the other party pursuant to the Agreement, unaltered by the receiving party, and created by the party/employees/contractually bound creators is within the definition. The out_not_sponsor_not_site text states such a case, but the predicate rejects it.

The out_not_delivered_by_party fact text is internally contradictory: it first states that Party A delivered the content to Party B pursuant to the Agreement, then states that it was not delivered by Party A to Party B. Its delivered_by_party_to_other=false coding cannot be determined from contradictory text.

Many fact vectors code negative facts not explicitly stated in their case text. For example, sponsor-delivery cases generally code is_proprietary_content_on_party_site=false without saying the content is not on Party A's Site; site cases code altered_by_receiving_party=false and pursuant_to_agreement=false without expressly stating those facts. A binary fact vector cannot treat unstated facts as explicit negatives.
The creator limitation is correctly modeled as applying to both the delivered-content and Site-content alternatives, and alteration is correctly limited to the delivered-content alternative.

The Boolean predicate faithfully captures the source’s inclusive category of enumerated agreements and amendments/modifications thereto, plus the written/oral, WYZZ-party-or-bound, WYZZ-TV relation/effect, and Effective-Date conditions.

The supplied quote does not define the capitalized term "Effective Date" or the identities/scope of WYZZ and WYZZ-TV. Those external definitions are required to apply the rule to real agreements and to support the cases’ asserted January 1, 2024 Effective Date.
The case texts explicitly state the facts encoded in their vectors; no case-level vector mismatch is identified.

The quoted definition incorporates the undefined external terms "Term," "Agreement," "Disclosing Party," and "Receiving Party." Their definitions are not supplied, so the source package is insufficient to determine their operative scope, although the proposed predicate faithfully preserves them as factual conditions.

The listed information categories (products, services, designs, methodologies, business plans, finances, marketing plans, customers or prospects, and Agreement terms) are illustrative because the source says "including"; correctly, the predicate does not make any category mandatory.
The predicate matches the quoted definition at the stated abstraction: Third Party AND acting under direction or control AND the directing/controlling entity is a Party.
c07 explicitly says Eta acts under the direction or control of no one, but codes acting_under_direction_or_control as true.

c08 says only that Theta is not acting under the direction or control of any Party. It does not establish that Theta is not acting under direction or control of a non-Party, so false/none is unsupported.

c14 states both direction by a Party and control by a non-Party. The single-valued directing_or_controlling_party field records only Party and omits the stated non-Party control; the fact model cannot faithfully represent this mixed fact.

The program identifies definitions of "Third Parties" and "Party" as dependencies, but those definitions are not included. Their contractual scope, including whether all entities labeled Party A through Party H qualify as a Party, cannot be verified from the supplied source.

The predicate omits two express requirements for products added by amendment: the product must be a product of the Company, and the addition must occur during the Contract Period. A signed written amendment alone is not sufficient under the quoted definition.

The program treats the signature requirement as merely a condition of the addition branch, but the source states that all amendments to the Agreement must be signed by all parties. The addition branch must require a Company product added during the Contract Period by a written amendment that satisfies this signature requirement.

Required facts and external source material are absent: whether an added product is a product of the Company, whether its amendment occurred during the Contract Period, and the executed amendments and agreement/addendum dates needed to establish those facts.

Cases c01-c07 and c13 code added_by_written_amendment=false and amendment_signed_by_all_parties=false even though their text states only logo use or non-use and does not explicitly state amendment facts.
Cases c08 and c10 code uses_pro_football_legends_logo_on_affixed_labels_hang_tags_or_packaging=false, but their text does not state whether the product uses the logo.
Case c09 codes negative amendment facts without stating them in the case text.
Case c11 codes amendment_signed_by_all_parties=false although the text states only that the product was not added by written amendment; it does not explicitly state that an amendment was unsigned.
The named-product branch is otherwise consistent with the quoted list and its logo-use qualification.

The source expressly says Product includes the 1000mg Formulation. The proposed predicate ignores is_1000mg_formulation and treats that reference as merely a nonoperative example. Without the definition or attributes of the referenced 1000mg Formulation, it cannot be established that the reference adds no independent inclusion or exception.
The required dependency/attachment for the capitalized term "1000mg Formulation" is absent. Its relationship to the preceding general description cannot be verified from the supplied quote alone.
For every listed non-1000mg case, is_1000mg_formulation is coded false, but the fact text does not explicitly state that the formulation is not the 1000mg Formulation.
In out_no_metformin, metformin_sole_active is coded false but is not expressly stated; it is only inferred from the statement that the tablet does not contain metformin.
